Ternivka New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Cherkasy Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This is the new Jewish cemetery of Ternivka, a companion to the Old and Oldest cemeteries documented elsewhere in this collection. Jews are first mentioned in Ternivka in 1765, growing to 2,823 people (more than half the town) by 1897, supported by a synagogue, three prayer houses, and a private Jewish boys' school by the early 20th century. Pogroms during WWI and the Russian Civil War claimed 11 Jewish lives. Under Soviet rule, a Jewish council, kolkhoz, and Yiddish school for 300 students were established, though all three synagogues were closed in 1935. Following the July 1941 German occupation, a ghetto held the town's entire Jewish population; almost all of Ternivka's Jews, along with others from the region totaling 2,300–2,500 people, perished in a mass killing on May 27, 1942, with the ghetto fully liquidated on April 2, 1943.
